children.name: Tetrachondra hamiltonii Petrie ex Oliv.
children.description: A creeping perennial herb (family Tetrachondraceae, order Lamiales) endemic to New Zealand, rooting at the nodes to form turf-like patches; stems are fleshy and square in cross-section, leaves opposite and fleshy (~2 x 2 mm), with solitary off-white to greenish-white flowers and fruit of four brown setulose nutlets. It grows in open damp turf along lake and tarn margins, flushes and seepages in the North and South Islands and Stewart Island. NZTCS: Threatened - Nationally Vulnerable.

children.name: Tetrachondra patagonica Skottsb.
children.description: An accepted species of Tetrachondraceae (order Lamiales), described by Carl Skottsberg in 1912 from southern South America. It is the South American vicariant of the otherwise New Zealand genus Tetrachondra, a small, low creeping or mat-forming perennial herb native to Patagonia and Tierra del Fuego.

children.name: Polypremum procumbens L.
children.description: Wet pine savannas (SPS-RF, VWLPS), adjacent roadsides.
